newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo 1996 trade deficit widens to $1.7 bln in Oct.
newsitem.headline: Yugo 1996 trade deficit widens to $1.7 bln in Oct.

text.p: Yugoslavia's 1996 trade deficit topped $1.7 billion in October, the Federal Statistics Office reported on Tuesday, and economists were puzzled by an unexpectedly strong rise in October imports.
Statistics showed 10-month exports grew to $1.425 billion while imports rose to $3.131 billion.
"The widening trade gap jeopardizes current economic performance and the dinar and price stability," Slobodan Milosavljevic of the Institute for Market Research told Reuters.
Milosavljevic said he was surprised by exceptionally strong growth in imports, adding that the level of the trade gap was worrying.
The central bank last reported its hard currency reserves mid-May, when they stood at $330 million.

"Officially, the huge imports are financed from companies' accounts abroad, but we seem to have underestimated those reserves," an economist said. "It would be good to know the exact figures on the country's official hard currency reserves."
Pavle Petrovic, chief economist of the private Institute for economic research CES-Mecon, said the problem of the trade deficit was a structural problem of the Yugoslav economy.
Petrovic insisted the deficit was needed to push the economy and to avoid stagnation and zero growth.
"A trade gap and a current account deficit are needed only to an extent allowing the Yugoslav economy to achieve some growth," Petrovic said.
But this huge trade gap is not justified, he said. If it maintains the strong upward trend, the government would need to adopt some measures to curb the deficit from rising, he said.
"This by no means implies returning to import controls. Those may slice the trade gap but also halt the economy," Petrovic said.

Economists said Yugoslav exporters still faced barriers in selling products abroad. They agreed exports would pick up only after Yugoslavia restores ties with international financial institutions and joins the World Trade Organisation. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
